The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century. One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonies in both cities.

According to video captured by the TV network pool, Hegseth was with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser and deputy assistant Tami Radabaugh walking up the steps in front of the memorial after posing for pictures. A laugh is audible, prompting the guard to yell: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” Hegseth looked over his shoulder in the direction of the soldier as he continued walking up the steps.

title: Ten Lives by Mona Chalabi review – what if we were totally honest about our wealth?
summary:
The data journalist puts her own finances – and those of ten others from across the economic spectrum – under a microscope

How much do you earn? If the question makes you bristle – and I realise we haven’t even met – would you answer it if someone convinced you that your candour might just change the world?

In her deliciously original first book, the former Guardian data journalist and illustrator Mona Chalabi sets out to do precisely that. The result – a dazzling mix of journalism, data visualisation and memoir – is both a joy to read and a serious provocation. Chalabi takes aim at our silence and furtiveness around individual income and finances. “Our collective ignorance is sustaining an unfair system,” she argues. Unless we talk more openly about our personal wealth, we will never be able to tackle the economic problems causing insecurity and anxiety for us all.

title: Amazon and Google Win Big From Anthropic IPO
summary:
If you’re looking for a cheaper way of getting exposure to Anthropic than buying the stock directly, consider Amazon or Google. Anthropic’s updated IPO filing on Tuesday shows just how many shares each of those two tech giants will own in Anthropic, along with how much money they’re making on their early investments in the AI firm.

Neither tech giant will own voting shares in Anthropic, so antitrust cops won’t have to worry about their influence over its management. But their stakes are significant. In theory, Amazon could own around 20% of Anthropic’s outstanding shares. But because of a self-imposed ownership cap, Amazon won’t hold more than 12% of Anthropic. The rest of its holdings are convertible notes that can convert to equity over time. Regardless, Amazon’s economic return is pretty damn good. title: Houseplant hacks: do you really need to feed your plants?
summary:
Some say their plants are fine without fertiliser, but are they just surviving when they could be thriving?

The problem
Enter a garden centre and you will be overwhelmed by a wall of feeds: liquid concentrates, slow-release, droplet bottles and specialist formulas for every plant going. Many people swear by them, while others say they have never fed their plants and they’re doing just fine. After all, plants in the wild manage perfectly well. So do our houseplants genuinely need feeding, or is it just consumerism?

The hack
Plants get energy from photosynthesis, but not minerals. They come from the soil, and in a houseplant bound by its pot that supply runs out over time. In the wild, roots roam through soil, fed constantly by decaying leaves, rain and living organisms. Adding fertiliser gives your plants the nourishment they need to grow and thrive.

title: The Command We Must Fund
summary:
The Army's Armored Force was born in July 1940, a few weeks after France fell. No act of Congress created it, and no budget line funded it. The Chief of Staff ordered it into being, took the tanks from the infantry and the cavalry, and placed them under a single commander. The money came later, once the force had demonstrated what it could do with what it already had. The idea had been waiting since 1928. The force did not wait for its appropriation.

Last week, I argued that the Autonomous Warfare Command could begin its work before it had a charter, a commander, or the $54 billion a reconciliation bill was supposed to deliver. This week, the bill lost its Congress. Democrats took both houses, and the two members who will now write the defense budget said what they think of the Pentagon's request within a day of the vote. A ‘mostly true’ tale of 19th-century sisters running from the law is underserved in a production stuffed with superfluous showboating

There, we meet two Black sisters, Mary and Martha Clarke, who will become wanted criminals. title: Dorgu rescues point for Manchester United in eight-goal thriller against Aston Villa
summary:
Does this late, late comeback draw keep Michael Carrick in his job? He urged United to back up their breathless Roma comeback victory on Tuesday by building momentum and they did, kind of, by avoiding defeat.

Patrick Dorgu’s 96th-minute equaliser went off his head and in. Senne Lammens, up for the corner, knocked into his opposite number, Zion Suzuki, but no foul was given – to Unai Emery’s disquiet, Aston Villa’s manager pointing to this afterwards. This made it 4-4 to follow Joshua Zirkzee’s added-time finish as Villa were somehow pulled back by Carrick’s chaotic unit.

title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary
summary:
President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters

Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).

Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.
